title: Champollion announces the decipherment of Egyptian hieroglyphs
summary: In 1822 the French scholar Jean-François Champollion announced that he had cracked hieroglyphic writing, in a letter to Bon-Joseph Dacier of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, presented in Paris on 27 September. It marked the birth of modern Egyptology; a fuller Précis du système hiéroglyphique followed in 1824.

uncertainty.note: The letter is dated 27 September 1822 (BCU Lausanne) and presented that day (History.com). National Geographic dates the breakthrough on the name Ramses to 14 September 1822, and another page (not used) gives 22 September for the letter.

where.historical_name: Paris, France, where the Académie royale des Inscriptions et belles-lettres met

importance.justification: The announcement that gave access to hieroglyphic documentation lost to reading since antiquity, described as the birth of modern Egyptology.

reviewer_note: Dates differ across pages (14, 22, 27 September); 27 September is used because two pages tie it to the letter or its presentation. The pin is Paris as a city, not a named building. Scope is the 1822 announcement only, not the Rosetta Stone itself.
